# Prerequisite tree: what you need to know to follow the proof

> **Work in progress, and still a map, not a check.** This tree is built from the Lean code, which has not been compiled or verified. Alpöge's promised write-up may organise the argument differently.

**Data:** [tree.yaml](tree.yaml) is the source of truth. **Diagram:** [TREE_GRAPH.md](TREE_GRAPH.md), generated by `scripts/tree_check.py`. This page is the readable walkthrough.

The idea: every step of the proof is a **node**. Each node lists what you must understand first (its **children**), until you reach things taught in school or in a first university course (**leaves**). Each node also says where to learn it: a textbook, a paper, or "only in this proof".

We fill this in top-down, easiest part first. The top layer (layer 1) is done below. It is the short, readable end of the proof.

**Leaves** (assumed known): school algebra, trigonometry, complex numbers (a + bi), basic calculus, infinite series, modular arithmetic.

**Status:** ✅ explained here · 📘 standard textbook material · 🔬 research literature · 🆕 only in this proof · ⬜ not mapped yet

---

## The shape of the proof, in one picture

```
RH  (Mathlib's statement)
└── L1  "no zeros right of ½" ⇒ RH          ✅  short, readable, about 60 lines
    ├── L1a  functional equation of ζ          📘  proved in Mathlib, not in this project
    ├── L1b  Γ has no zeros; cos zeros         📘
    └── L2  "no zeros right of ½" for every Dirichlet L-function   ⬜ ← the whole hard part
            (UpperTheory.EveryCharacter)
```

Nearly all of the 175,000 files exist to prove **L2**. Layer 1 shows that L2 really does imply RH, and you can follow it with first-course maths.

---

## Node RH: the statement

**In plain English:** ζ(s) is the zeta function. If ζ(s) = 0, s is not one of the "trivial" zeros (−2, −4, −6, …), and s ≠ 1, then the real part of s is exactly ½.

**Lean:** `Main.lean:4`. The definition is Mathlib's `RiemannHypothesis`, not the project's own.

**Children:**
- **RH.1 ζ for Re s > 1:** ζ(s) = 1 + 1/2ˢ + 1/3ˢ + … — **needs:** complex powers (school complex numbers + exp/log), convergent series. 📘
- **RH.2 Analytic continuation:** the series only makes sense for Re s > 1. Complex analysis extends ζ to every s ≠ 1, and that extension is the ζ in RH — **needs:** a first course in complex analysis (holomorphic functions, power series, uniqueness of continuation). 📘
- **RH.3 Trivial zeros:** why −2, −4, … are zeros. This falls out of L1a.

**Learn it from:**
- *Gentle:* J. Derbyshire, *Prime Obsession* (popular, no prerequisites).
- *Real:* Stein & Shakarchi, *Complex Analysis*, ch. 1–3 and 6.
- *Number-theory view:* Apostol, *Introduction to Analytic Number Theory*, ch. 11–12.

## Node L1: "no zeros right of ½" ⇒ RH ✅

**Lean:** `Formalism/GammaFactorNonvanishing/RhOfRight.lean:5` (`rh_of_right`), which `CritLine.lean:29` (`rh_of_every`) and `Supplements/Kernels/MainTheorems.lean:9` (`rhOfAll`) both call.

**The argument in plain English:**
1. Suppose ζ has no zeros with real part > ½ (apart from the pole at s = 1). Take any non-trivial zero s.
2. If Re s > ½, that contradicts the assumption.
3. If Re s < ½, look at 1 − s, whose real part is > ½. The functional equation (L1a) gives

   ζ(s) = 2 · (2π)^(s−1) · Γ(1−s) · cos(π(1−s)/2) · ζ(1−s).

   The left side is 0. The factors 2, (2π)^(s−1) and Γ(1−s) are never 0 here. The cosine is 0 only when s is a trivial zero, which is excluded. So ζ(1−s) = 0, and 1 − s is a zero with real part > ½, a contradiction.
4. So Re s = ½.

This is a **symmetry argument**. Zeros come in mirror pairs s ↔ 1 − s, so ruling out the right half also rules out the left half. That is why the whole project only needs to prove L2.

**Children:**
- **L1a Functional equation of ζ** 📘. Mathlib's `riemannZeta_one_sub`, used here, not proved by this project. To *use* it you only need algebra. To *prove* it you need the Gamma function, the theta function and Poisson summation (Fourier analysis). Sources: Stein & Shakarchi, *Complex Analysis*, ch. 6; *Fourier Analysis*, ch. 4–5; Edwards, *Riemann's Zeta Function*, ch. 1.
- **L1b The factors are finite and nonzero** 📘. Γ(z) is never 0 (it has no zeros at all, only poles). cos(z) = 0 exactly when z = π/2 + kπ, which is school trigonometry extended to complex z. Mathlib: `Complex.Gamma_ne_zero_of_re_pos`, `Complex.cos_eq_zero_iff`. Source: Stein & Shakarchi, *Complex Analysis*, ch. 6.1 (the Gamma function).
- **L1c Case analysis on Re s < ½, = ½, > ½** ✅. School algebra and inequalities. Most of the 60 lines handle edge cases like s = 0 or k ≤ 0.

## Node L1′: the same trick for Dirichlet L-functions ✅

**Lean:** `Formalism/GammaFactorNonvanishing/CritLine.lean:11` (`critLine`), giving the "generalised RH" (GRH) results in `Main.lean`.

**In plain English:** the same mirror argument works for every **primitive** Dirichlet L-function, using its own functional equation. The mirror of χ is χ̄ (its complex conjugate), so the hypothesis must cover all characters, not just one.

**Children:**
- **D1 Dirichlet characters** 📘. A function χ on whole numbers that repeats every N steps and is multiplicative: χ(ab) = χ(a)χ(b). Formally, a homomorphism (ℤ/Nℤ)ˣ → ℂˣ. **Needs:** modular arithmetic (leaf), and groups and homomorphisms from a first abstract-algebra course. Source: Apostol, ch. 6; any intro algebra text, e.g. Pinter, *A Book of Abstract Algebra*.
- **D2 L(χ, s) = Σ χ(n)/nˢ** 📘. Like ζ, with a twist by χ. ζ is the case N = 1 (`LFunction_modOne_eq`). Source: Apostol, ch. 6–7 and 12.
- **D3 Primitive characters and conductor** 📘. A character is "primitive" if it doesn't secretly come from a smaller N. The functional equation is cleanest for primitive χ. Source: Davenport, *Multiplicative Number Theory*, ch. 5.
- **D4 Functional equation of L(χ, s)** 📘. The completed function Λ(χ, s) = Γℝ-factor × L(χ, s) satisfies Λ(χ, 1−s) = ε · Λ(χ̄, s). The Γℝ-factor depends on whether χ is even or odd (`gammaFactor_ne_zero`, `CritLine.lean:6`). Mathlib: `completedLFunction_one_sub`. Source: Davenport, ch. 9.

## Node L2: "no zeros right of ½" for every Dirichlet L-function ⬜

**Statement** (`Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/CharacterBoxes/EveryCharacter.lean:13`): for every N, every Dirichlet character χ mod N, and every s with Re s > ½: L(χ, s) ≠ 0 (except the pole of ζ at s = 1).

This is **the actual content of the claimed proof**. Its first children, as named in the code (`MainConclusion.lean:7-14`), are below. Names are the code's own, and the descriptions are guesses until someone reads the files.

| Child (Lean name) | Folder | Guess at meaning | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.every_character_of_literature_of_vWin` | `AutomorphicArithmetic/ThetaCorrespondence/…` | L2 follows from a package of results from the literature plus a condition called "VWin" | ⬜ |
| `UpperTheory.Zero.LLC.recTExists` | `AutomorphicArithmetic/Foundations/LocalLanglands/…` | an existence statement in the **local Langlands correspondence** ("LLC") | ⬜ 🔬 |
| `UpperTheory.Gal.Int.galoisLocalGlobalStrong_recParameter` | `AutomorphicArithmetic/Foundations/GaloisRepresentations/…` | a local–global compatibility statement for **Galois representations** | ⬜ 🔬 |
| `UpperTheory.One.vwin_of_row` | `AutomorphicArithmetic/AutomorphicVarieties/ModularityArgument/…` | a **modularity** argument giving "VWin" | ⬜ |

Even the folder names say this layer needs graduate-level machinery: automorphic forms, the theta correspondence, Galois representations, local Langlands, modularity. Mapping it is the next job.
